:::{#exm-two-part-description-length}
#### The two-part description lengths of coin flips

<!-- no-figure: the example is a table of description lengths -->

A coin is flipped $100$ times and lands heads $70$ times.
The code below follows @def-two-part-description-length
with nine models,
the Bernoulli models with the probability of heads $0.1, 0.2, \ldots, 0.9$.
It gives each model a codeword of the same length,
and it prints the two parts and their sum for each model.

```{r}
#| label: two-part-description-length
n_flips <- 100
n_heads <- 70
success_prob <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1)
model_bits <- log2(length(success_prob))
heads_bits <- n_heads * log2(success_prob)
tails_bits <- (n_flips - n_heads) * log2(1 - success_prob)
data_bits <- -(heads_bits + tails_bits)
total_bits <- model_bits + data_bits
data.frame(success_prob, model_bits, data_bits, total_bits)
```

Each model takes $`r round(model_bits, 2)`$ bits to name,
because nine equally long codewords need $\log_2 9$ bits.
The data part is smallest, at $`r round(min(data_bits), 1)`$ bits,
for the model with probability of heads $`r success_prob[which.min(data_bits)]`$.

:::
